name: Paris
hook: The city Jeopardy returns to for the Seine, the Louvre and the Eiffel Tower.

facts.label: the Seine
facts.statement: The Seine flows through Paris; the city bought the land at its source and erected a statue of the goddess Sequana.

facts.label: the Louvre
facts.statement: The Louvre began as Philip Augustus's castle and was renamed the Musée Napoléon under Napoleon.

facts.label: Notre-Dame
facts.statement: Pope Alexander III laid Notre-Dame's cornerstone in 1163; Victor Hugo's 1831 novel gave it the bell ringer Quasimodo.

facts.label: the Eiffel Tower
facts.statement: The Eiffel Tower was the gateway to the 1889 International Exhibition; con man Victor Lustig sold it for scrap twice.

facts.label: the Bastille
facts.statement: The Bastille's first stone was laid in 1370; the Paris Metro station named for it recalls the French Revolution.

facts.label: the Sorbonne
facts.statement: The Sorbonne began as a 1250s theology school founded by Robert de Sorbon and has more than 750 years of history.

facts.label: The Phantom of the Opera
facts.statement: Gaston Leroux's 1910 novel The Phantom of the Opera is set in the Palais Garnier; a real 1896 chandelier accident inspired it.
